# escalate-government-legal

> Communications from Hungarian government agencies, tax authority, legal entities, and regulatory bodies get immediate triage — missed deadlines carry real consequences for the new Kft.

## Trigger and action

**When:** Fires when an email arrives from government domains (tarhely.gov.hu, nav.gov.hu), legal/accounting entities, or contains regulatory deadline language.
**Then:** Route to priority triage with deadline-extraction context; flag any date-sensitive content and create a review errand.

## Rationale

The 'Administrative Debt Backlog' and 'Hungary-UK-US Legal Complexity' patterns converge on a single risk: David is operating across three legal jurisdictions (Hungary, US, UK) in the most compliance-intensive phase of his founder journey. Szabó-Stubán Kft was founded April 22-May 2, 2026 — just six weeks ago. The first year of a Hungarian Kft under KIVA requires NAV filings, FEOR compliance, monthly guaranteed minimum wage calculations, and quarterly reporting. Missing any of these creates fines that compound.

Simultaneously, he has 41 tarhely.gov.hu emails (government digital mailbox), an overdue Diákhitel (student loan), Ugly Code LLC's Wyoming annual report due, and ongoing correspondence with accountants transitioning from RetconLine to Olive & Brown. The property purchase at Kondorosi út adds notary appointments and contract deadlines.

Unlike newsletters or GitHub noise, government/legal emails have hard deadlines with real penalties. A NAV filing reminder buried under 444.hu articles could cost thousands in fines. This instinct ensures every government or legal communication surfaces to triage immediately, regardless of how busy the inbox is.

## Examples

- Tárhely (tarhely.gov.hu) notification about new NAV document — immediate triage
- Olive & Brown sends KIVA quarterly filing reminder — priority triage with deadline flag
- Diákhitel overdue payment notice — triage (legacy debt but regulatory consequence)
- Firstbase reminder about Ugly Code LLC annual report deadline — triage with US jurisdiction context
